answer.rationale: p99 latency spike of 5x target coincides with release 2 hours ago. During settlement peak with heavy writes, this timing correlation is strong. memory_b1 demonstrates rollback cleared a checkout error spike without customer impact; memory_b2 shows regional failover creates write-loss risk during hot write periods (the exact condition we have now). memory_b6 confirms staged gating catches regressions, suggesting this release may not have had sufficient pre-flight validation. Rollback is the only action that directly addresses potential bad code while preserving write safety. Circuit breakers and read replicas don't fix latency sources; capacity takes time we don't have; failover explicitly risks writes during peak settlement. Rollback the recent release first, preserve data integrity, then assess if secondary interventions are needed.
